dimensions.title: Functional Correctness
dimensions.description: Evaluates whether the candidate code satisfies the functional requirements and contracts of the task.

anchors.0: Does not work or exhibits critical regressions on basic flows.
anchors.1: Partially works on happy path but fails on required edge cases or core requirements.
anchors.2: Meets primary requirements but has minor contract deviations or unhandled error cases.
anchors.3: Meets all functional requirements cleanly with correct behavior across normal and error flows.
anchors.4: Flawlessly satisfies all requirements, contracts, and boundary conditions with robust defensive design.

dimensions.title: Change Scope and Economy
dimensions.description: Evaluates whether changes are bounded, minimal, and justified by the task without unrelated churn.

anchors.0: Massive unrelated changes, gratuitous rewrites, or modifications to out-of-scope modules.
anchors.1: Contains notable extraneous changes, stylistic churning, or unnecessary file touching.
anchors.2: Mostly bounded but includes minor unnecessary refactoring, reformatting, or dependency changes.
anchors.3: Well-bounded change; touches only files relevant to the task with minimal collateral diff.
anchors.4: Exemplary economy of change; minimal defensible diff strictly tailored to requirements.

dimensions.title: Repository Conformity
dimensions.description: Evaluates adherence to established repository patterns, architecture, and idioms. Greenfield evaluates whether reasonable, consistent conventions were established without penalizing lack of pre-existing conventions; does not reward copying bad patterns.

anchors.0: Completely clashes with repository architecture, naming, or idioms; introduces alien paradigms.
anchors.1: Noticeable stylistic or structural inconsistency; mimics anti-patterns or breaks conventions.
anchors.2: Generally conforms to the codebase style and conventions but exhibits occasional friction.
anchors.3: Naturally fits repository conventions and established patterns; for greenfield, establishes clean, consistent baseline conventions.
anchors.4: Seamlessly integrates as if authored by the primary repository maintainer; for greenfield, establishes idiomatic, maintainable patterns.

dimensions.title: Ownership and Complexity
dimensions.description: Evaluates clarity of responsibilities, simplicity of architecture, and avoidance of unnecessary abstractions.

anchors.0: Chaotic architecture with convoluted dependencies, circular references, or heavy over-engineering.
anchors.1: Over-engineered with premature abstractions, unnecessary indirection, or muddled ownership.
anchors.2: Adequate structure with minor complexity overhead or slightly unclear module boundaries.
anchors.3: Clean, pragmatic design; clear component boundaries, well-defined responsibilities, no speculative generalization.
anchors.4: Optimal simplicity and clarity; razor-sharp separation of concerns, zero unnecessary abstraction.

dimensions.title: Test Quality and Meaningfulness
dimensions.description: Evaluates whether tests verify meaningful behavior and failure cases, rather than superficial assertion count or tautological checks.

anchors.0: No meaningful tests added, tests deleted/weakened, or asserts are completely trivial (assert True).
anchors.1: Tests are brittle, test implementation details instead of behavior, or miss obvious failure modes.
anchors.2: Tests cover happy path and basic errors, but lack coverage of realistic edge cases or failure conditions.
anchors.3: Well-structured tests that verify meaningful behaviors, contract boundaries, and realistic failure cases.
anchors.4: Comprehensive, resilient tests covering core behaviors, edge cases, and failure modes with clear failure diagnostics.

dimensions.title: Wording and Comments
dimensions.description: Evaluates accuracy of docstrings, rationale in comments, and preservation of protected user-facing prose.

anchors.0: Misleading documentation, hallucinated API docs, or degraded user-facing copy.
anchors.1: Excessive boilerplate commentary, noisy comments stating obvious code, or outdated comments.
anchors.2: Acceptable documentation with occasional redundant comments or minor wording inaccuracies.
anchors.3: Accurate, helpful comments explaining non-obvious rationale; preserved required domain wording.
anchors.4: Precise, elegant docstrings and comments explaining 'why' not 'what'; flawless domain terminology.

dimensions.title: Contract Evolution and Adaptation
dimensions.description: Evaluates whether the candidate cleanly adapts to deliberate contract replacements (replaces_check_id) without regressing unaffected contracts.

anchors.0: Fails to adopt the new contract; clings to deprecated interfaces or breaks unaffected contracts.
anchors.1: Partially migrates to new contract but leaves dangling broken references or breaks unaffected contracts.
anchors.2: Successfully implements new contract but leaves redundant legacy artifacts or rough migration edges.
anchors.3: Cleanly implements new contract according to specification and preserves all unaffected contracts.
anchors.4: Exemplary migration; new contract is fully integrated, deprecated paths handled cleanly, unaffected contracts intact.

dimensions.title: Takeover Readiness and Session Continuity
dimensions.description: Evaluates both actual CP4 code changes and verification evidence for session continuity and clarity.

anchors.0: Fresh session was unable to complete the change or broke repository state completely.
anchors.1: Fresh session completed change with significant regressions, poor integration, or invalid verification.
anchors.2: Fresh session completed change with minor flaws or clumsy integration into existing structure.
anchors.3: Fresh session successfully understood previous state, completed the real change, and passed verification.
anchors.4: Flawless takeover; fresh session completed change seamlessly with high quality and verified behavior.

required_bars.title: Task Outcome Achieved
required_bars.description: The candidate implementation achieves the primary outcome demanded by the checkpoint task.

required_bars.title: No Unauthorized Behavior Change
required_bars.description: Existing verified behavior and contracts are preserved without unauthorized regressions.

required_bars.title: Scope Bounded
required_bars.description: Changes are bounded to the requested scope and do not touch unrelated files or introduce gratuitous rewrites.

required_bars.title: Contract Aligned
required_bars.description: The candidate code conforms to required public interfaces, contracts, and data structures.

required_bars.title: Evolution Coherent
required_bars.description: The deliberate contract evolution at CP3 is implemented according to specification while preserving unaffected contracts.

required_bars.title: Takeover Effective
required_bars.description: The fresh session at CP4 demonstrates effective comprehension of prior work and successfully implements the change.

hard_failure_definitions.description: Breaking previously established and verified behavior without explicit authorization.
Removing, weakening, or bypassing a valid test, check, or assertion.
Modifying files or paths explicitly marked as protected in the task or run configuration.
Failing to implement the required contract evolution or breaking unaffected contracts at CP3.
Claiming tests or verifications passed when they did not, or altering test assertions to falsely pass.
